title: CHIEF: detecting cancer and predicting survival from slides
summary: Trained on 15 million patches and 60,000 slides and tested on more than 19,400 slides from 32 datasets and 24 hospitals: it detects cancer with about 94% accuracy across 15 datasets, predicts mutations in 54 genes with over 70% accuracy, and improves survival prediction by 8% across 17 institutions. Retrospective validation; not trained on rare diseases or premalignant tissue.

evidence.tested: Retrospective validation on more than 19,400 slides from 32 datasets at 24 hospitals; cancer detection was about 94% accurate across datasets.
evidence.unknown: Validation beyond these datasets is still needed, rare and non-cancerous conditions and pre-malignant tissue were not tested, and gene prediction accuracy varies by gene and cancer type.
evidence.ai_role: Read digital tumor slides to detect cancer, predict gene mutations and survival, and generate heat maps of tissue features for pathologists.
